---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/getfider/fider
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: getfider/fider pinned by digest (see quirks; there are no version tags)
  port: 3000
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: fider
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ NO MAIL RELAY MEANS A SITE NOBODY CAN SIGN INTO, INCLUDING ITS OWNER. THIS IS THE FIRST THING TO SETTLE WITH THE USER, BEFORE THE PLAN. Fider is passwordless by design: there is no password field anywhere. Signing in sends a link or a code by e-mail, and creating the very first account works the same way (app/handlers/signup.go dispatches SendSignUpEmail and the site stays PENDING until the link in it is clicked). So collect working SMTP credentials FIRST. The failure has two shapes and only one of them is loud: with no mail variables at all the process refuses to start, because app/pkg/env/env.go:184-206 infers EMAIL=smtp and then requires EMAIL_SMTP_HOST and EMAIL_SMTP_PORT; with WRONG ones it boots perfectly, serves a beautiful signup page, and silently never delivers anything. Do not deploy this app hoping to add mail afterwards."
  - "SMTP DETAILS THAT DECIDE WHETHER MAIL ACTUALLY LEAVES THE VM. Set EMAIL_NOREPLY to an address your relay is allowed to send AS, or the relay accepts the connection and rejects the message. Use a submission port: 587 with EMAIL_SMTP_ENABLE_STARTTLS (already the default, env.go:126), or 465 with EMAIL_SMTP_ENABLE_IMPLICIT_TLS=true. Do NOT plan on port 25 outbound: it is blocked by default on most clouds and a self-hosted mail server needs PTR control this deployment does not have. EMAIL_SMTP_USERNAME and EMAIL_SMTP_PASSWORD may legitimately be empty for an internal relay, which is why they are not in the required list; for any real provider they are not. Mailgun (EMAIL_MAILGUN_API + EMAIL_MAILGUN_DOMAIN) and SES (EMAIL_AWSSES_REGION + key pair) are the other two supported types and each has its own required set."
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: THE FIRST PERSON TO COMPLETE THE SIGNUP FORM, AND A STRANGER DOING IT DOES NOT JUST TAKE THE SITE, IT BRICKS IT. Verified in app/handlers/signup.go:46-80: CreateTenant assigns enum.RoleAdministrator to the account being created. In single-host mode GET /signup redirects to / the moment ANY tenant exists (signup.go:130-145), so the claim is ONE-SHOT. Worse, the tenant row is written as PENDING before the e-mail is verified, and app/middlewares/tenant.go:94-107 then serves the Pending Activation page on EVERY route: a drive-by claim by someone whose verification link goes to THEIR inbox leaves the instance permanently stuck on that page, recoverable only by deleting the tenant row in Postgres by hand. So the deploy is not finished when the URL answers. Claim the site in the same session, before you hand the URL to anyone, and confirm the e-mail address with the user first."
  - "⛔ REGISTRATION IS OPEN AFTER THE FIRST ACCOUNT, AND THE SETTING THAT CLOSES IT IS NOT AN ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE. On a public tenant any e-mail address can sign itself in and is created as enum.RoleVisitor (app/handlers/signin.go:225-245). The switch is the tenant's IsPrivate flag: with it on, app/middlewares/tenant.go:110-114 sends unauthenticated visitors to /signin and signin.go:145 refuses new users with 403. It lives at Administration then Privacy in the UI, or POST /_api/admin/settings/privacy, and it needs an authenticated administrator session, so it is a STEP IN THE DEPLOY after claiming the account, not a variable you can set up front. Ask the user which they want: a public board that customers can join is the normal way to run Fider, and a private one is normal for an internal roadmap."
  - "SIGNUP_DISABLED=true IS NOT THE ANSWER, AND SETTING IT EARLY LOCKS YOU OUT. It makes both GET /signup and POST /_api/tenants return 404 (app/handlers/signup.go:48,132), which on a fresh single-host instance means YOU cannot create the first account either. It is meant for multi-tenant hosts. Leave it unset for the deploy, claim the site, then close the door with the privacy setting above."
  - "⛔ SET JWT_SECRET AND REUSE THE SAME VALUE ON EVERY REDEPLOY. It is tagged required (app/pkg/env/env.go:56) so the app will not start without one, which is the good half. The bad half is what happens if you generate a fresh one on a redeploy: it signs the session cookies AND the sign-in and verification links that are Fider's only authentication mechanism, so every logged-in user is thrown out and every e-mail link that has not been clicked yet becomes invalid, including the one your first admin may still be waiting for. Generate one long random value, hand it to the user, and pass the same one forever."
  - "DATABASE: ONE URL, NO SQLITE, NO SECOND DATABASE. app/pkg/env/env.go:73 reads DATABASE_URL and it is required, so there is no silent local-file fallback to guard against here: without it the container panics on boot, loudly. deploy_compose with database:'managed' appends PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD and a ready-made DATABASE_URL to the project .env and never edits your compose, so either pass ${DATABASE_URL} straight through or, when you want to be explicit about TLS, build it yourself: postgres://${PGUSER}:[REDACTED:conn-password]@${PGHOST}:${PGPORT}/${PGDATABASE}?sslmode=require. Fider needs exactly ONE database, and it creates no second one, so redu's one-database-per-managed-server rule never bites here."
  - "DO NOT OVERRIDE THE CONTAINER COMMAND, BECAUSE THE MIGRATIONS ARE IN IT. Dockerfile:67 is `CMD ./fider migrate && ./fider`. Replace it with a bare ./fider and the schema is never created; the app then fails against an empty database in a way that reads like a connection problem. There is no separate migrate_command to configure: leave the image's own command alone. PROVE IT BOTH WAYS AFTER BOOT: GET /_health must return 200 with status Healthy (that handler pings the database, app/handlers/common.go:27-35, so it is the positive half AND the database check in one), and the managed database must list Fider's tables. If the health call did not succeed, an empty table listing tells you nothing."
  - "NO VOLUME, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. BLOB_STORAGE defaults to `sql` (app/pkg/env/env.go:130), so the logo, uploaded images and attachments are stored as rows in Postgres. That makes the managed database the ONLY durable state in this deployment, which is simple and back-up-able, and it also means image-heavy boards grow the database rather than a disk. If you deliberately switch BLOB_STORAGE to fs you must set BLOB_STORAGE_FS_PATH and mount a volume on it, or every upload dies at the next redeploy."
  - "⛔ THERE IS NO VERSION TAG TO PIN, SO PIN THE DIGEST. Measured on the Docker Hub API on 2026-08-17: getfider/fider has no 0.36.1, no v0.36.1 and not even a `latest`; all three 404. What exists is `stable`, `main`, PR_<number> and SHA_<commit>. And they disagree: with one identical Accept header, `stable` resolves to sha256:«REDACTED:longhex:ca409521» (pushed 2026-07-06) while «REDACTED:entropy:25a5f91c», built from the exact commit the v0.36.1 git tag points at, resolves to sha256:«REDACTED:longhex:871b829e». Use the release one: image getfider/fider:«REDACTED:entropy:25a5f91c»@sha256:«REDACTED:longhex:871b829e». A digest is the only pin here that means anything, and never write a bare rolling tag into a recipe a stranger runs."
  - "⛔ DO NOT ADAPT THEIR docker-compose.yml. IT DOES NOT CONTAIN FIDER. Read it: mailhog, a postgres:17 called pgdev, a second one called pgtest, and a minio, all for running their test suite. There is no app service in it at all. Write a one-service compose yourself against the image above. Anyone who copies that file onto a VM gets three containers, none of which is the product, and a Postgres with a documented password on it."
  - "PORT 3000, SET BASE_URL, AND GENERATE THE HOSTNAME YOURSELF. env.go:50 defaults PORT to 3000 and Dockerfile:63 exposes it. BASE_URL is mandatory in single-host mode (env.go:170-179) and it is used to build every link that goes out by e-mail, so a wrong value produces sign-in links pointing somewhere else, which is a locked-out user rather than a cosmetic bug. Generate the dname yourself in full `fider-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so BASE_URL is known at deploy time, and give it as https://<that>, with no trailing slash."
  - "LEAVE ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK_TARGETS AT FALSE. It defaults to false (env.go:59) and it is the guard that stops Fider's webhooks and OAuth URL fetches from reaching private addresses. On redu the private network it would reach into contains your own managed database VM, so turning it on to make some internal integration work converts the instance into an SSRF probe inside your own infrastructure. If a user genuinely needs it, that is a conversation, not a default."
  - "SIZING IS REASONING, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Upstream publishes no memory figure (checked README, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml). m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB) is chosen because Fider is NOT a plain Go binary: go.mod pulls in rogchap.com/v8go, an embedded V8, and server-side renders every page through it, so it carries a JavaScript heap in-process the way a Node app would. m1.small would probably serve a quiet board and is the obvious thing to try on the first real deploy; m1.medium is the honest default until somebody measures it. Write the number back here when you do, because nobody upstream has published one."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> collect the SMTP settings from the user FIRST -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.045/hr, roughly GBP 33 a month, inside the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; omitting db_flavor_id defaults the database VM to the app flavor and doubles the bill), port 3000 -> then claim the administrator account before handing over the URL."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built: the image is pulled. Write the one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. Pointing deploy_compose at their GitHub URL would try to build a Go server, a V8 binding and a webpack UI on the VM, which takes a very long time and produces the same image you can pull in seconds."
  - "LICENCE: AGPL-3.0, AND THE THIRD-PARTY METADATA THAT SAYS MIT IS WRONG. The LICENSE file in the repo is the GNU Affero GPL v3, verbatim. For a self-hoster the clause that matters is SECTION 13: if you modify Fider and let people use it over a network, you must offer THOSE USERS the corresponding source of your modified version. Running the unmodified official image does not create new work here beyond the notices the image already carries, and pointing at github.com/getfider/fider is the honest answer if anyone asks. The obligation lands on whoever OPERATES the service, which is the user, not redu. If they intend to patch it, tell them the source-offer applies to their patched version."
  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, ON PURPOSE. delete_deployment removes the app VM but keeps the managed Postgres, and for this app that database is EVERYTHING: posts, votes, comments, accounts and every uploaded image. It keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. To stop paying entirely the user must also delete_database, and that is irreversible."
---

# Self-host Fider on redu

A public feedback board where your users post ideas, vote on them and see what you are building:

If a stranger claims it and never verifies, every route serves "Pending Activation" forever and the only fix is deleting a row in Postgres by hand. So the address has to be one whose inbox you can open in the next few minutes.

3. **Privacy** — safe to default to public (that's how Fider is normally run) and flip later; it's a UI/API setting, not an env var, so it costs nothing to change afterwards.

4. **Drive mode** — I default to guided regardless, so this one is really just "do you want the cost checkpoint or not."

Yes — verified against the pinned commit, not from memory. Here's the real picture.

**Simply omitting mail doesn't work**, and that's the trap `redu.md` describes: with no mail vars the container won't boot, and with dummy ones it boots and nobody — including you — can ever sign in.

**But there's a second authentication path that needs no mail at all: OAuth.** What I confirmed in the source:

- `EMAIL` (`env.go:107`) accepts `smtp`/`mailgun`/`awsses`, and the validation switch has **no default case** — so `EMAIL=none` passes with zero mail variables set. It boots.
- Each backend's `Enabled()` compares the type to its own name (`smtp.go:41`), so none register. Mail is sent through `bus.Publish` listeners, and `bus.go:144-153` loops over an empty listener slice — a silent no-op, not a crash.
- GitHub/Google/Facebook are enabled by the presence of a client ID alone (`oauth.go:56-61`), with no DB rows and no tenant, and `renderer.go:191-197` lists them for any unauthenticated visitor — so the buttons appear on a fresh `/signup`.
- The decisive line is `signup.go:53-56`: `socialSignUp := action.Token != ""` sets the tenant to **Active, not Pending**, registers the admin with the OAuth identity, and sets the auth cookie immediately (`signup.go:82-99`). No verification e-mail exists in that path.

That last point is a bonus: **the "stranger bricks your instance on Pending Activation" failure mode disappears**, because it only exists on the e-mail path.

content.text:
**Callback URL is `https://<your-host>/oauth/github/callback`** (`routes.go:88`) — I generate the hostname before deploying, so I can hand you that exact URL up front.

So the shape is: `EMAIL=none`, `EMAIL_NOREPLY` set to any address (it's tagged `required` but nothing sends), plus one OAuth client ID/secret pair. No relay, no domain verification, no SPF/DKIM.

**The honest trade-offs:**

| | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Not *zero* setup | You register an OAuth app — GitHub takes about two minutes, free, no DNS involved. Much lighter than a mail relay, but not nothing. |
| Who can join | Everyone needs an account with that provider. Fine for a developer-facing roadmap; narrower than "any e-mail address" for general customers. |
| Notifications | "Someone commented on your post" e-mails silently won't send. In-app notifications still work. Invite-by-e-mail is dead. |
| Reversible | Adding SMTP later is an env change plus redeploy — provided `JWT_SECRET` stays identical. Nothing here is one-way. |

One caveat I won't paper over: `EMAIL=none` works because that switch has no default case, which is undocumented rather than a supported "disable mail" flag. Pinning the digest means it can't shift under us. The documented-shape alternative is a dummy SMTP host, which also boots — but then every send attempt actually runs and fails, which is just log noise for the same result.

Use a submission port: 587 with EMAIL_SMTP_ENABLE_STARTTLS (already the default, env.go:126), or 465 with EMAIL_SMTP_ENABLE_IMPLICIT_TLS=true. Do NOT plan on port 25 outbound: it is blocked by default on most clouds and a self-hosted mail server needs PTR control this deployment does not have. EMAIL_SMTP_USERNAME and EMAIL_SMTP_PASSWORD may legitimately be empty for an internal relay, which is why they are not in the required list; for any real provider they are not. In single-host mode GET /signup redirects to / the moment ANY tenant exists (signup.go:130-145), so the claim is ONE-SHOT. Worse, the tenant row is written as PENDING before the e-mail is verified, and app/middlewares/tenant.go:94-107 then serves the Pending Activation page on EVERY route: a drive-by claim by someone whose verification link goes to THEIR inbox leaves the instance permanently stuck on that page, recoverable only by deleting the tenant row in Postgres by hand. # Self-host Fider on redu

A public feedback board where your users post ideas, vote on them and see what you are building:
one Go container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL.

About GBP 0.045/hour, roughly GBP 33 a month. Inside the no-card free trial.

## Before you deploy: Fider has no passwords

Fider signs people in **by e-mail**. There is no password field anywhere in it, and the very first
account, the one that owns the site, is created by clicking a link in an e-mail too.

**So a Fider with no working mail relay is a site that nobody can ever log into, including you.**
Have SMTP credentials ready before you start: a host, a port (587 or 465, not 25), and a from
address the relay will let you send as. Any transactional provider works; the recipe does not care
which.

## What this deploys

- **Fider** from the official image, pinned **by digest** (there are no version tags), on one
  m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM. It holds everything, including uploaded images.
- No volume, on purpose: Fider's default blob storage is the database.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Fider on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**The signup race, which is worse here than elsewhere.** The first person to complete the form
becomes the administrator, and the tenant row is written *before* the e-mail is verified. A
stranger who claims your fresh instance and never clicks their link leaves it stuck on "Pending
Activation" on every route, with the signup page redirecting away. Recovering that means deleting
a row in Postgres by hand. Claim the site in the same session that deploys it.

**Silent mail.** Wrong SMTP settings start cleanly and deliver nothing. The only proof that mail
works is that a verification e-mail actually arrived.

**The image tag.** `getfider/fider` publishes no version tags at all, not even `latest`.
`stable` and the release commit's build are different images. Pin the digest.

## Verify it after boot

Run this from your machine. It refuses to pass when it cannot tell.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# HOST=fider-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud ./verify.sh
set -u
: "${HOST:?set HOST to the public hostname}"

body=$(mktemp)
code=$(curl -sS -o "$body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/_health")

if [ "$code" = "502" ] || [ "$code" = "503" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the edge answered $code, which is what redu serves while a container is"
  echo "still starting. Re-run in a minute rather than reading this as a failure."
  rm -f "$body"; exit 2
fi
[ "$code" = "200" ] || { echo "FAIL: /_health answered $code"; rm -f "$body"; exit 1; }

# Positive control FIRST. This handler pings Postgres before answering, so a match proves both
# that we are talking to Fider and that its database is reachable. Every check below is
# meaningless without it.
grep -q 'Healthy' "$body" || {
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: HTTP 200 but the body is not Fider's health document"
  rm -f "$body"; exit 2; }
rm -f "$body"

# Now the ownership question. Polarity matters and it is the opposite of what you would guess:
# on an UNCLAIMED single-host instance GET /signup answers 200 and serves the form to anyone.
# Once a site exists the handler redirects to / with 307. So 200 here is the ALARM.
signup=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/signup")
case "$signup" in
  200)
    echo "FAIL: /signup is serving the form, so this instance is UNCLAIMED. Whoever loads it"
    echo "first becomes the administrator, and a claim they never verify leaves the site stuck"
    echo "on Pending Activation. Claim it now; do not publish the URL."
    exit 1 ;;
  30*)
    echo "OK: /signup redirects, so the site has been claimed." ;;
  *)
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /signup answered $signup, which is neither the form nor the redirect."
    exit 2 ;;
esac

echo "OK: Fider is up, its database is reachable, and the administrator seat is taken."
echo "Mail is NOT tested here and cannot be: the only proof is a verification e-mail arriving."
```

Fider is **AGPL-3.0** (third-party catalogues that say MIT are wrong; read the LICENSE file).
